Topic: Quantum Superposition and the Nature of Quantum States

Target audience: University students (Introductory Physics/Computer Science)

Section: section_1 — The Classical vs. Quantum Divide

Lecture lines:
Classical bits are either zero or one.
Quantum systems allow simultaneous states.
Imagine a dial, not a switch.
This is a complex vector space.
The qubit is our fundamental unit.

Planned animations:
Show binary '0' and '1' blocks in #FF4500 (OrangeRed).
Display a vector in a 2D complex plane with color #00CED1 (DarkTurquoise).
Transition vector to represent state |ψ⟩ in #FFFF00 (Yellow).
Highlight vector length as 1 unit in #FFFFFF (White).
Label the state as 'Qubit' in #00FF00 (Lime).

Section: section_2 — Visualizing Superposition

Lecture lines:
We use the Bloch Sphere visualization.
Quantum states are vectors on it.
Superposition is defined by alpha and beta.
Think of a spinning coin blur.
Vectors represent $|\psi\rangle = \alpha|0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle$.

Planned animations:
Draw a 3D sphere outline in #FFFFFF (White) with coordinate axes.
Display a vector |ψ⟩ pointing to a point on the surface in #FFD700 (Gold).
Show the combination of |0⟩ and |1⟩ as MathTex in #00CED1 (DarkTurquoise).
Animate vector rotating on the sphere's surface in #FFD700 (Gold).
Highlight coefficients α and β in #FFFF00 (Yellow).

Section: section_3 — The Measurement Problem

Lecture lines:
Observation triggers wavefunction collapse.
Measurement yields definite states.
Probabilities are alpha and beta squared.

Planned animations:
Show the superposition state |ψ⟩ as a vibrant wave in #FF4500 (OrangeRed).
Animate the wave collapsing to state |0⟩ or |1⟩ in #FFFFFF (White).
Display probabilities |α|² and |β|² as MathTex in #00FF00 (Lime).

Section: section_4 — Quantum Parallelism (Application)

Lecture lines:
Superposition enables massive quantum parallelism.
Process multiple states simultaneously.
Quantum efficiency exceeds classical limits.

Planned animations:
Visualize two parallel computational paths in #00CED1 (DarkTurquoise).
Show both paths being processed simultaneously in #FFFF00 (Yellow).
Highlight the exponential density growth in #FF4500 (OrangeRed).

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
